subject.title: Add native PowerShell smoke coverage for contributor commands

question: Should OpenClaw add recurring native PowerShell smoke coverage now, and should that first lane include `pnpm build:strict-smoke` or only commands already proven stable under Windows `pwsh`?
rationale: The requested coverage fits the test-infrastructure roadmap, but it changes recurring Windows CI scope and the active candidate shows the selected build-smoke command still needs proof or narrowing.

options.title: Fix and prove full smoke
options.body: Keep the requested `check:docs` plus `build:strict-smoke` coverage, but merge only after the exact Windows `pwsh` lane is green with redacted proof.

options.title: Land a narrower first lane
options.body: Start with the native PowerShell command or commands that already pass, and leave build-smoke coverage as follow-up work.

options.title: Defer recurring Windows smoke
options.body: Keep the issue open but postpone a recurring PowerShell smoke lane until runner budget or release priorities justify it.

recommendation.title: Fix and prove full smoke
recommendation.body: Keep the requested `check:docs` plus `build:strict-smoke` coverage, but merge only after the exact Windows `pwsh` lane is green with redacted proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent overlap across CI stabilization and the PowerShell-safe docs tooling adjacent to this issue.
